chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a mutamattiʿ who finds the price but does not find sheep, he said: He should leave the price with some of the people of Mecca and instruct one who will buy for him and slaughter on his behalf, and that suffices for him. فإذا مضى ذو الحجة، he delays that until the coming year in Dhū al-Ḥijjah.

key_terms.الثَّمَنَ: the price or monetary value used to purchase the sacrificial animal
key_terms.الْغَنَمَ: sheep, referring here to the sacrificial animal
key_terms.ذُو الْحِجَّةِ: the month of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, the time connected to the hajj sacrifice
key_terms.يُجْزِي: it suffices or fulfills the obligation

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim performing tamattuʿ do if he has the money for the hady but cannot find an animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a pilgrim performing tamattuʿ who possesses the money for the sacrificial animal but cannot find the animal itself. He may entrust the money to someone in Mecca to purchase and slaughter on his behalf, and if Dhū al-Ḥijjah passes, the sacrifice is deferred until the next Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
